h1: 8 Carpet Cleaners and Stain Fighters for Pet Households, Ranked & Reviewed (2026)
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 8 pet carpet cleaners, from upright deep cleaners to portable spot machines and enzyme sprays, compared by type and price.
mainKeyword: carpet cleaners for pet hair and stains
summary: The BISSELL ProHeat 2X Revolution Pet Pro Plus is the deep cleaner to buy for a house with shedding dogs and repeat accidents, thanks to its pet formula and a full-size upright build. The Shark CarpetXpert HairPro is the strongest rival for hair, the BISSELL TurboClean PET covers the mid-price slot, and the Shark StainStriker is the best portable for sofas and stairs.
intro: The common mistake with pet carpet cleaners is treating the stain you can see and ignoring the one you cannot. Urine soaks through the carpet into the pad below, and surface scrubbing leaves the proteins that make the smell come back every humid day. A machine that rinses and extracts is half the answer; the other half is a cleaner that breaks those compounds down.

So this ranking mixes two kinds of product on purpose: upright and portable machines that extract, and two enzyme or pet-formula sprays that treat the stain chemistry. We reviewed them on paper, from listings, noting form factor, whether a pet formula is named and the price bracket. None publishes tank size or suction in the facts we used, so we do not invent them.

products.name: BISSELL ProHeat 2X Revolution Pet Pro Plus Carpet Cleaner
products.verdict: A full-size heated deep cleaner with a pet formula for the worst households.
products.description:
The ProHeat 2X Revolution Pet Pro Plus is the flagship in this ranking. It is a full-size machine paired with a pet formula, and sits in the $200 to $500 bracket. The ProHeat line is known for heating the water as it cleans, which helps loosen set-in stains.

It ranks first because it is the most complete answer to both hair and stains. A full-size upright covers whole rooms in far fewer passes than a portable, and a pet formula targets the odors that standard shampoo leaves behind. The tradeoff is size and cost, since it is the heaviest and most expensive tool here and demands storage space.

Buy it if you have several pets or large areas of carpet. Skip it if you have a small apartment and only need spot treatment.
products.idealFor: Multi-pet homes with large carpeted areas.
products.skipIf: You live in a small apartment with a few rugs.

products.name: Shark CarpetXpert HairPro StainStriker Carpet & Stain Cleaner
products.verdict: An upright that adds hair management to Shark's stain-focused cleaning.
products.description:
The CarpetXpert HairPro is an upright carpet cleaner combining Shark's StainStriker stain system with a HairPro design aimed at the tangles pets leave. It sits in the $200 to $500 bracket, level with the ProHeat.

It ranks second because pet hair is the common failure of deep cleaners: long hair wraps around the brush and kills suction. A hair-focused design addresses that directly. It sits behind the ProHeat because the listing names no pet formula or heating, and the BISSELL's focus on odors is better suited to repeated accidents.

Choose it for shedding breeds on thick carpet. Skip it if odor from accidents is your main concern.
cons: Priced the same as the ProHeat
products.idealFor: Homes with long-haired or heavy-shedding pets.
products.skipIf: Urine odor is your biggest problem.

products.name: BISSELL TurboClean PET
products.verdict: A pet-branded upright for $100 to $200, half the cost of the flagships.
products.description:
The TurboClean PET is an upright carpet cleaner in the $100 to $200 bracket, branded for pets. It brings the BISSELL name to a price that suits a one-pet household.

It ranks third because a full-size upright for roughly half the cost of the top two is strong value, though without the heating of the ProHeat or the hair design of the Shark. It edges its standard sibling since the PET label signals a pet-oriented formula or accessories.

Buy it if you want a full-size cleaner without the flagship price. Skip it if you fight heavy, set-in stains.
pros: Full-size upright at a mid price
Good for one or two pets
products.idealFor: One- or two-pet homes needing a full-size cleaner.
products.skipIf: You have deep, set-in urine stains.

products.name: BISSELL TurboClean Upright Carpet Cleaner
products.verdict: The non-PET sibling, at the same price bracket.
products.description:
The TurboClean Upright Carpet Cleaner is the standard version of the PET model, also in the $100 to $200 bracket. It offers the same BISSELL upright format, without a pet label.

It ranks fourth because the PET edition costs the same and signals pet-oriented extras. If you can find this standard model for less, the tradeoff disappears. It remains a competent upright for general carpet cleaning.

It makes sense if you find it discounted or you only need general carpet care. Skip it if pet messes are a weekly occurrence.
cons: Same price as the PET model
products.idealFor: General carpet care in homes with light pet use.

products.name: Shark StainStriker HairPro Portable Stain Cleaner
products.verdict: A portable stain machine for stairs, sofas and car seats.
products.description:
The StainStriker HairPro is a portable stain cleaner in the $100 to $200 bracket. Portables spray, scrub and suction a small area, which makes them ideal for upholstery and stairs where an upright cannot go.

It ranks fifth because pet owners need the portable as a companion more than as a replacement. It cleans fresh accidents quickly but cannot do a whole living room. It beats the Hoover since the HairPro name suggests attention to hair handling.

Buy it for accidents on stairs, couches and car seats. Skip it if you need to deep clean wall-to-wall carpet.
products.idealFor: Spot cleaning stairs, furniture and car seats.

products.name: Hoover PowerDash Pet Compact Carpet Cleaner Machine
products.verdict: A compact pet-edition machine for small rooms and rugs.
products.description:
The PowerDash Pet is a compact, portable carpet cleaner in the $100 to $200 bracket, aimed at pet owners. It is smaller than an upright, so it handles rugs, small rooms and stairs.

It ranks sixth because compact machines trade tank size for storage, which means more refills. It is stronger than the sprays below for deep cleaning, but less capable than the uprights for whole-house use.

It suits apartments and renters with a few rugs. Skip it if you have wall-to-wall carpet in several rooms.
products.idealFor: Apartment owners with rugs and a pet.

products.name: Rocco & Roxie Supply Co. Rocco & Roxie Enzyme Stain & Odor Eliminator
products.verdict: An enzyme formula for the proteins behind urine odor, under $25.
products.description:
The Rocco & Roxie is an enzyme stain and odor eliminator costing under $25. Enzyme cleaners use biological compounds to break down the proteins in urine, vomit and feces, rather than covering the smell.

It ranks seventh because it is not a machine and cannot lift hair or deep-clean a room. It earns its spot because pairing an enzyme spray with any extractor above is how you stop repeat marking. It outranks the Resolve spray in this guide for its enzyme focus.

Buy it as a companion to a carpet cleaner. Skip it as your only tool.
pros: Works on fresh and old stains
products.skipIf: You need a machine to clean whole rooms.

products.name: Resolve Ultra Pet Carpet Cleaner Spray - for Removal of Pet Stains &
products.verdict: A pet-formula spray for quick stain removal, under $25.
products.description:
The Resolve Ultra Pet is a pet-formula carpet cleaner spray priced under $25. It is aimed at fresh stains, applied directly and blotted.

It ranks last because it treats the surface and does not extract moisture from deep within a carpet. It does offer instant convenience, with no setup or refill required.

Keep a bottle for quick fixes. Skip it if you want to eliminate odor from soaked pads.
cons: Cannot deep clean on its own
products.idealFor: Quick cleanup of fresh pet stains.
products.skipIf: Odor has soaked into the pad.

methodology.title: Cleaning approach
methodology.description: Uprights, portables and sprays were separated by what each can clean, from whole rooms to a single spot.

methodology.title: Pet formula and enzymes
methodology.description: A named pet formula or enzyme chemistry was weighed because odors need more than water.

methodology.title: Hair handling
methodology.description: Designs that mention hair management were credited, since tangles are a common failure mode.

methodology.title: Brand support
methodology.description: Service networks and parts availability from BISSELL, Shark and Hoover were counted in favor.

methodology.title: Value within the bracket
methodology.description: Each product was set against the under $25, $100 to $200 or $200 to $500 bucket where it competes.

whatMatters.detail: Uprights clean whole rooms, portables handle stairs and furniture, and sprays treat a single spot. Pick the form that matches where accidents actually happen. A portable is rarely enough for wall-to-wall carpet.
Enzyme cleaners break down the proteins in pet waste, while ordinary soap just lifts surface dirt. Urine odor returns without enzymes. Look for the word enzyme on the label or a pet-specific formula.
Long hair wraps around brush rolls and chokes suction in an ordinary carpet cleaner. A hair-focused design, like the HairPro, tackles this. Check for a brush that can be cleaned out easily.
Warm water loosens set-in stains and dissolves oils better than cold. Heated models cost more but improve results on old messes. Look for ProHeat or a heater on the listing.
Overwet carpet takes hours to dry and can grow mildew. A strong extraction and a large tank reduce refills and drying time. Check owner feedback on how damp the carpet stays after cleaning.

faq.q: Can I use enzyme spray with a carpet cleaning machine?
faq.a: Yes. Apply the enzyme spray to the stain, let it sit as directed and then extract with the machine. Avoid mixing different cleaners in the tank unless the manufacturer allows it.

faq.q: What is the biggest mistake when cleaning pet stains?
faq.a: Using a standard soap-based cleaner or steam first. Heat can set protein stains, so treat with an enzyme cleaner before any steam or hot water.

faq.q: Is the ProHeat worth it over the TurboClean PET?
faq.a: If you have several pets or old set-in stains, yes. For one pet and occasional accidents, the TurboClean PET does most of the work for half the price.

faq.q: How do I set up an upright carpet cleaner?
faq.a: Fill the clean tank with water and the recommended solution, vacuum the carpet first to remove loose hair, then work in overlapping passes. Avoid soaking the floor.

faq.q: How do I maintain a carpet cleaner?
faq.a: Empty and rinse both tanks after each use, clear hair from the brush roll and let all parts air dry. This prevents mildew and odor.
Portable models like the Shark StainStriker and Hoover PowerDash are made for upholstery. Uprights are too big, so check fabric care tags before cleaning.

finalTake: The BISSELL ProHeat 2X Revolution Pet Pro Plus is the carpet cleaner to buy for a busy pet household. The Shark CarpetXpert HairPro takes the hair-heavy homes, and the BISSELL TurboClean PET is the sensible mid-price upright. Whatever machine you choose, keep an enzyme spray on the shelf for accidents.
